gaps.sentence: The manager, for ___ the team played so hard, thanked everyone.
gaps.hint: played for the manager — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: The preposition 'for' demands the object form 'whom' for a person.

gaps.sentence: The chair on ___ the cat was sleeping was my grandmother's.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern for things; 'on where' and 'on that' are not grammatical.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.
'What I meant' means 'the thing that I meant'; 'that I meant' would be an incomplete relative clause.

gaps.sentence: The degree to ___ the climate is changing alarms scientists.
gaps.explanation: 'The degree to which ...' is a formal pattern used with abstract nouns; 'that' cannot follow the preposition.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.
